title: Personality Theories: Psychodynamic, Humanistic & Big Five
description: Explore Freud's psychoanalytic defense mechanisms, Carl Rogers, and the Big Five OCEAN trait taxonomy.

slides.title: Freud's Structural Personality Model 🧊
slides.content:
# The Psychodynamic Mind

Sigmund Freud conceptualized the mind as an iceberg composed of three conflicting agencies:

* **Id**: Completely unconscious; operates on the **Pleasure Principle**, demanding immediate gratification of primal biological drives (eros and thanatos).
* **Ego**: Largely conscious; operates on the **Reality Principle**, mediating between the impulsive demands of the Id and the realistic constraints of the world.
* **Superego**: Our internalized moral conscience, striving for perfection and generating feelings of guilt or pride.

quizData.question: An aggressive individual who harbors deep unconscious hostile impulses becomes a champion competitive boxer, channeling that aggression into an admired sport. Which Freudian defense mechanism is this?
quizData.explanation: Sublimation is redirecting unacceptable instinctual desires into socially constructive and culturally valued activities.

slides.title: Humanistic Perspectives on Personality 🌱
slides.content:
## Carl Rogers & Self-Actualization

Humanists rejected Freud's dark determinism and behaviorist mechanization, emphasizing conscious free will and innate human growth.

* **Self-Actualization** (Abraham Maslow): The ultimate psychological drive to fulfill one's authentic unique potential.
* **Carl Rogers' Person-Centered Theory**:
  * **Self-Concept**: Our organized set of beliefs about our own nature and qualities.
  * **Congruence vs. Incongruence**: Harmony between our actual self and our idealized self.
  * **Unconditional Positive Regard**: Complete acceptance and love without contingent conditions, essential for healthy personality maturation.

slides.title: The Big Five Trait Model (OCEAN) 🌊
slides.content:
## The Contemporary Gold Standard in Trait Psychology

Personality traits are enduring behavioral patterns. Factor analysis across diverse global cultures converged on the **Five-Factor Model (OCEAN)**:

| Trait | High Scorers | Low Scorers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Openness** | Creative, intellectually curious, adventurous | Conventional, routine-oriented, pragmatic |
| **Conscientiousness** | Organized, disciplined, goal-directed, reliable | Careless, spontaneous, disorganized |
| **Extraversion** | Outgoing, energetic, talkative, assertive | Reserved, reflective, quiet, introverted |
| **Agreeableness** | Empathetic, trusting, helpful, cooperative | Skeptical, competitive, critical, blunt |
| **Neuroticism** | Anxious, emotionally reactive, prone to worry | Emotionally stable, calm, composed under stress |

quizData.question: A person who is highly reliable, meticulously keeps track of deadlines, maintains an organized schedule, and thinks before acting scores high on which Big Five dimension?
quizData.explanation: Conscientiousness reflects self-discipline, organization, dutifulness, and goal-directed persistence.

slides.title: Biological Basis of Personality 🧬
slides.content:
## Heritability of Traits

Longitudinal studies of identical twins reared apart indicate that Big Five traits possess an estimated **40% to 50% genetic heritability**, and show remarkable stability across adulthood from age 30 into older age.
